In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-terminal 20-40 amino acids of Xcv HrpB2 are sufficient for the translocation of effector proteins into the cytoplasm of host and nonhost plants.
HrpB is essential for T3S of effectors in X. campestri pv. vesicatoris.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HrpB is an inner rod component of the T3S apparatus of Xanthomonas that is essential for the translocation of effector proteins into the plant cell.
HrpB1 and HrpB2 are the first two inner rod proteins of a bacterial T3S apparatus for which the secretion signal is identified.
the HpaABC regulon controls the T3S and subsequent translocation of Hrp2 into plant cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T3SS of X. campetris pv. vesiciatoria can be reprogrammed to translocate effecotr proteins in a nonpathogen.
the secretion of HrpB proteins is tightly controlled by the HpaC switch protein, which suppresses the secretion of HrcU and HrpB2 but promotes the secretion of translocons and effectors.
the N-terminal domain of HrpB is a promising target to interfere with the pathogenicity of Xanthomonas species.
